You let the packet rest open before you and listen.

Ashara lifts one page from hers. “I want the assessment criteria before any placements are assigned.”

Ashworth nods as if he expected it. “You’ll have them this morning. Briefs are assessed for accuracy, judgment, and whether the writer understands the limits of their authority. Placement reports are assessed the same way.”

“And Rowan’s separate programme?” Rashid asks. “Is that assessed by the same standard?”

“The same academic standard,” Ashworth says. “A different practical arrangement. There is no human delegation to receive a first-year observer.”

Rashid looks down at his papers. “That doesn’t make the gap disappear.”

“No,” Ashworth says. “It does not.”

Aldric shifts in his chair. “It does give him a way to begin closing it.”

Ashara glances at him. “If the work is real.”

“It will be,” Ashworth says, with enough edge to end the exchange.

He distributes another sheet: seminar rooms, faculty hours, dueling-ground rules, library access, and the house regulations governing guests after midnight. Thessaly reads the guest section twice, then folds the page neatly into thirds.

“Now,” Ashworth says, “we’ll cover the less glamorous matter of how to ask for help before a problem becomes public.”
